newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq warns of power cuts.
newsitem.headline: Iraq warns of power cuts.

text.p: Iraq has warned of Baghdad power cuts lasting up to three hours a day, saying its power generation is deteriorating because of a lack of spare parts.
The Iraqi media has urged families to ration the use of power in the home and shops have been told to use fewer lights and electrical applicances.

A timetable issued by the Baghdad Power Distribution Department (BPDD) sets out the cuts in different areas of the capital for the rest of the year with the worst cuts in August when temperatures and consumption soar.
"In order to secure a just distribution of electricty for all citizens, a programme for periodic cuts is adopted," director-general of electricity Sahban Faisel said in remarks published on Monday.

Iraq's power stations were bombed by the U.S.-led multinational force which pushed Iraqi troops out of Kuwait in 1991. Iraq says that 90 per cent of the damage has been repaired but it still needs spare parts to operate stations at full capacity.
Power cuts increased recently due to what Faisel said were "severe shortages of spare parts."

Under a deal with the United Nations allowing limited oil sales to pay for essential goods, Iraq is allowed to import spare parts for its national grid but it complains that none have reached the country so far.
